instruction: SAFETY/BYPASS R1 review of WP-SCP-022 slice 020P (RULE-001 Phase 2 — implement SCP-R-004 + cut v1.1.0) at branch feature/wp-scp-022-020p-scp-r-004-implementation, HEAD commit `9f8639d`. Stress-test the safety/bypass posture of the implementation. Specifically: (1) The new WARN_BASELINE_RULES = {'SCP-R-004'} set in .github/workflows/policy-check.yml is the most consequential safety surface. Verify: (a) the set is a strict allow-list (only rules explicitly in the set get warn-baseline rendering); (b) SCP-R-001/002/003 continue to render as ::error:: + count toward effective_denies + trip threshold; (c) no path exists where an adopter could rename their rule to 'SCP-R-004' and get warn-baseline treatment for a deny-class rule (rule_id is set by the rule's Rego file, not by adopter input — verify); (d) the bypass-pairing.sh + waiver-suppression mechanism continues to work for SCP-R-004 (waivers + rule-config can suppress); (e) what happens if a future SCP-R-NNN rule's _id collides with 'SCP-R-004' through an adopter's policy fork (verify the WARN_BASELINE_RULES set is a SCP-self-only constant in policy-check.yml, not adopter-overridable). (2) The own-predicates posture in policies/SCP-R-004.rego: SAFE-MAJ-001 closure was the rule defining its own scp_r_004_is_waiver_payload + scp_r_004_has_nonempty_string. Verify the implementation actually defines these own predicates rather than calling scp_r_002_*. Verify there is no remaining cross-rule reference to scp_r_002_* anywhere in SCP-R-004.rego. Verify the predicates are functionally equivalent to SCP-R-002's per the SAFE-MAJ-001 closure intent (semantically identical, semantically isolated). (3) The meta-waiver posture: §5 SAFE-MIN-001 closure documented that meta-waivers MUST themselves contain a URL. Verify the test_scp_r_004_waiver_suppresses_deny test in policies/tests/scp_r_004_test.rego correctly exercises this — the meta-waiver's reason in the test contains 'https://github.com/.../issues/100'. Verify there is no test that demonstrates a URL-less meta-waiver suppressing SCP-R-004 (which would contradict the §5 closure). (4) The residual-bypass per RULE-001 §5 case 5: 'https://x' satisfies the rule. Verify there is no test that asserts 'https://x' should DENY (which would contradict the residual-bypass acknowledgement). Verify the regex `https?://[^\s]+` accepts 'https://x' (does it? `[^\s]+` requires at least one non-whitespace char after the scheme; 'https://x' has 'x' after the scheme — yes, matches. Confirm.). (5) The truncation: verify scp_r_004_truncate_reason cannot leak the full reason text through some edge case (e.g. if reason contains a U+2026 already, does the truncation predicate still apply correctly? If reason is exactly 80 chars, which branch fires?). Edge case: if reason is exactly 80 chars (`count(reason) == 80`), the predicate `count(reason) <= 80` matches and returns reason as-is. Correct (no truncation needed). If reason is 81 chars, returns substring(0, 79) + ellipsis. Verify both branches are mutually exclusive (no overlap). (6) The conflict-gate Python evaluator: verify URL_PATTERN.search() (not URL_PATTERN.match()) is used — search matches anywhere in the string, mirroring Rego regex.match anchoring semantics. (7) Workflow-level escaping: the warn-baseline branch emits ::warning:: with `print(f"::warning file={location},title={structured['rule_id']}::{structured['message']}{suffix}")`. If structured['message'] contains a `::` substring or a newline, could it inject malicious workflow-command syntax? Verify the GitHub workflow-command syntax handling — typically GitHub strips/escapes embedded :: but the safe pattern is to not allow attacker-controlled content into annotation messages. Adopters control their waivers.json content; an adopter could craft a waiver entry whose `reason` contains `::error file=.github/workflows/policy-check.yml,title=SCP-E001::malicious-message` to inject a workflow command. Is this a vulnerability? (Probably not because GitHub Actions only interprets workflow commands written to stdout by the workflow itself, not echoed values from input files — but verify this assumption.) (8) The v1.1.0 release notes claim 'no behavioural change' for adopters whose waivers all already include URLs. Verify this is accurate by reading v1.0.1 release notes for comparison. (9) ADOPT-001 §12.7.14 'Option A — Gradual amendment' says SCP-R-004 fires on each waiver entry without a URL. Verify this is operationally correct — what if an adopter has 50 waivers and 45 have no URL? They get 45 ::warning:: annotations. Is this overwhelming? Should the rule rate-limit? (Probably acceptable — the messages are per-entry as designed; rate-limiting would lose information.) (10) The promotion path warning in §12.7.14: 'Adopters relying on Option B's rule-config disable should remove the disable before the promotion lands.' Verify this is consistent with the existing rule-config disable + one-release-grace behaviour (per ADOPT-001 §12.7.7 SCP-E006). (11) Verify the residual-bypass framing in RULE-TEMPLATE.md amendment is honest — it says 'no NEW bypass mechanism is introduced' vs 'no possible bypass exists'. Is this distinction reviewable? Could a future RFC author exploit this distinction to slip in an actual new bypass under cover of 'residual'? (12) Verify no new SCP-EXXX infrastructure code is claimed (the v1.1.0 release notes assert this). NEVER recommend descoping; propose inline-fix or file as TF-020P-NNN. Output to docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/dispatches/020p/review-safety.json.
